one_liner: Binance offers a broad, free REST/WebSocket API for spot, futures, wallet and more using self-generated HMAC-signed API keys, plus an official vendor-hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: Users create an API key and secret in API Management. Private endpoints need HMAC-SHA256 signed requests, with the key sent in the X-MBX-APIKEY header. The draft claim that OAuth (Binance Login) is partner-only could not be confirmed from the fetched pages, so it is unverified. The official MCP server uses a browser authentication flow with scopes.
access_notes: Any Binance account can create an API key for free. Public market data endpoints need no key. A Spot testnet is listed on a third-party pricing profile. Partner programs (CAAS, Institutional Buy/Sell) are gated, but they are not needed for the core API.
blocker_notes: Per-user API keys with HMAC signing mean there is no self-serve OAuth for multi-user access. This is a design consideration, not a blocker.
